Section 1
General Information

The SNG 270-E Prototype is a hybrid electric platform combining the Sur-Ron Light Bee X chassis with Husqvarna-style ergonomics and KTM-spec suspension. This manual provides complete assembly, service, and maintenance procedures for the prototype configuration. Built specifically for riders 6'0"–7'0", the 270-E addresses the geometry gap in the electric off-road segment with full-size MX wheel fitment, extended swingarm, and a raised seat system delivering a 39.5" seat height on the Sur-Ron platform.

Section 2
Safety Notices & Warnings

HIGH VOLTAGE WARNING — Disconnect the 72V battery before performing any service. High-voltage components must be handled with insulated tools at all times.

  • Disconnect the 72V battery before performing any service
  • High-voltage components must be handled with insulated tools
  • Use only torque-rated fasteners and apply Loctite where specified
  • Verify wheel alignment before riding
  • After any chassis modification, perform a full geometry check

5.1 — Disassembly

Powertrain Installation
6.1 — Motor Installation
Sotion FW01 Motor — 26–40kW
  1. Position motor in OEM cradle
  2. Install mounting bolts with blue Loctite
  3. Torque to 40–45 Nm
  4. Verify rotor clearance
6.2 — Jackshaft Installation
Warp9 Jackshaft
  1. Align sprocket with rear sprocket plane
  2. Torque jackshaft bolts to 25 Nm
6.3 — Controller Installation
BAC8000
  1. Mount using L-brackets or custom plate
  2. Route phase wires away from frame edges
  3. Pre-load Sotion FW01 map
6.4 — Battery Installation
72V Pack
  1. Install foam isolation pads
  2. Secure pack under KTM tank cover
6.5 — Chain Drive
GritShift Chain Drive Conversion · RK 420 Gold Chain · 54T Rear Sprocket
  1. Install GritShift Heavy Hitter chain drive conversion kit
  2. Install 54T sprocket on rear wheel
  3. Fit RK 420 gold chain — cut to length after wheelbase is set
  4. Set chain slack to 25–30 mm

270-E Step-by-Step Build
Rev 1.0
Stage 1 — Frame Preparation & Thermal Head Tube Fit

Before bolting on any heavy powertrain components, you must establish the modified structural chassis geometry. Because you are mixing the Ultra Bee subframe and Husqvarna ergonomics onto an LBX main frame, precise fitment here is critical.

1.1 — Thermal Fit Head Tube Conversion
  1. Freeze the Cups: Wrap your GritShift WP85 conversion cups in a clean plastic bag (to keep moisture off them) and place them in a freezer for at least 1–2 hours. Freezing causes the aluminum to microscopically contract.
  2. Clean the Head Tube: Thoroughly clean the inside of the Sur-Ron LBX head tube with brake cleaner or degreaser. Ensure it is entirely free of old grease, dirt, or factory burrs.
  3. Heat the Frame: Right before installation, take a heat gun (or propane torch, keeping the flame moving) and evenly heat the outside of the frame's head tube. It should be hot to the touch, but not smoking hot.
  4. The Drop-In: Grab a frozen cup, apply a very thin layer of anti-seize or waterproof grease to the mating surfaces, and quickly square it up to the heated head tube.
  5. Seat Home: Due to the extreme temperature differential, the cup should slide in almost entirely by hand or require significantly less force with your bearing press tool. Work quickly before temperatures equalize. Ensure there is absolutely no gap between the lip of the cup and the frame. Repeat for the opposite side.
1.2 — SKR Subframe Modification & Rivnut Installation
  1. Position the Ultra Bee Subframe against the LBX main frame mounting nodes. Mark the exact locations where the frame needs to be drilled for the new mounting points to achieve the "2" Up / 2" Back" tall-rider geometry.
  2. Use a center punch on your marks, then drill the holes matching the outer diameter specification of your heavy-duty rivnuts.
  3. Thread a rivnut onto your rivnut tool, insert it completely flush into the drilled hole, and compress the tool to deform and lock the rivnut into the frame. Repeat for all subframe mounting points.
  4. Offer up the subframe to the newly installed rivnuts. Thread the structural bolts in hand-tight only for now to allow for alignment wiggle room later.
1.3 — Foot Peg Assembly
  1. Slide the Prickly Extra-Wide Foot Pegs into the factory LBX peg brackets.
  2. Install the return springs, ensuring the long arm rests flat against the frame anchor point.
  3. Push the peg pins through, apply blue Loctite to the securing threads, and torque tightly. Verify both pegs snap back cleanly when lifted.

Stage 2 — Powertrain & Primary Drive Installation

Installing the motor and jackshaft while the frame is stripped gives you maximum clearance for tools and hands.

[BAC8000 Controller] ---> Mounted to front/top plate
       |
  (Phase Wires)
       v
[Sotion FW01 Motor] ----> Primary Drive ----> [Warp9 Jackshaft]
2.1 — Sotion FW01 Motor Installation
  1. Lift the Sotion FW01 motor into the factory LBX engine cradle. Support the bottom with a mechanical scissor jack or block of wood from underneath.
  2. Align the factory mounting holes. Slide the main motor mounting bolts through from the left side to the right.
  3. Apply blue Loctite to the threads.
  4. Using a torque wrench, cross-torque the bolts progressively to 40–45 Nm.
  5. Install the Prickly Motor Cover over the exposed motor faces using the provided small hex hardware.
2.2 — Warp9 Jackshaft Installation
  1. Insert the Warp9 Jackshaft assembly through the main frame pivot housing.
  2. Before tightening, visually align the inner primary drive sprocket with the Sotion motor's output sprocket. They must sit on a perfectly parallel plane.
  3. Apply blue Loctite to the jackshaft retention bolts and torque to 25 Nm.
2.3 — BAC8000 Controller Mounting
  1. Affix your custom mounting plate or L-brackets to the upper frame down-tube section.
  2. Secure the BAC8000 Controller onto the brackets. Ensure the heavy-gauge terminal side points toward the motor/battery cavity.
  3. Route the three heavy phase wires (Blue, Green, Yellow) down to the Sotion motor terminals.
  4. Connect the motor encoder/hall sensor wiring harness directly into the matching waterproof plug on the BAC8000 loom.

⚠️ Chafe Warning: Use heavy-duty zip ties and rubber routing wrap anywhere these phase cables pass near sharp aluminum frame edges. The extreme vibration from a 40kW system can cause raw metal to cut through cable insulation over time.

Stage 3 — Front & Rear Suspension Systems
3.1 — Front Fork Assembly (WP XACT 85)
  1. Grease the steering stem bearings of your KTM 85 triple clamps thoroughly with high-pressure waterproof grease.
  2. Drop the lower bearing onto the stem, slide the stem up through your newly installed GritShift head tube conversion cups, and install the upper bearing, dust seal, and top clamp nut. Tighten the stem nut until all play is gone, but steering still sweeps smoothly without binding.
  3. Slide the WP XACT 85 Fork legs up through the triple clamps. Position them so the top caps are flush with or slightly protruding above the top triple clamp.
  4. Torque the triple clamp pinch bolts to 18–22 Nm in an alternating pattern.

3.2 — Rear Shock & Extended Swingarm
  1. Line up your Custom Extended Swingarm with the frame's main pivot bore.
  2. Coat the Titanium Swingarm Bolt lightly with anti-seize or grease, slide it all the way through the frame and swingarm bearings, and torque the nut to 55–60 Nm.
  3. Install the 1.5" Shock Riser Bracket to the upper factory shock mount node on the frame. Torque its retention bolt to 35 Nm.
  4. Position the EBMX Rear Shock inside the frame. Bolt the top eyelet to your new riser bracket, and bolt the bottom eyelet to the swingarm linkage progression triangles. Torque both shock bolts to 30 Nm.
Stage 4 — Wheels, Braking & Final Drive Line
4.1 — Wheel Mockup
  1. Front Wheel: Fit the Flow Wheels KTM 85 21" front wheel between the WP XACT fork legs using the Flow Wheels Fork Adapter Kit. Slide the KTM 85 axle through, seat it completely, and tighten the axle pinch bolts on the bottom of the fork lugs.
  2. Rear Wheel: Slide your 54T Rear Sprocket onto the Flow Wheels 18" rear wheel hub and torque the sprocket bolts to 25 Nm using blue Loctite. Slide the rear wheel axle assembly into the slots of your extended swingarm. Leave the axle nut loose for now.
4.2 — GritShift Heavy Hitter Chain Drive Conversion
  1. Wrap the heavy-duty RK 420 Gold MX Chain around the jackshaft output sprocket and back over your 54T rear sprocket.
  2. Pull the rear wheel back along the extended swingarm adjusters until you reach your target wheelbase length (56.5–57 inches).
  3. Mark the exact link on the chain where it overlaps cleanly. Use your chain breaker tool to push out the rivet pin at that mark, breaking the chain to your exact custom length.
  4. Join the chain ends together using the master link and press the clip on securely — ensure the closed end of the clip faces the direction of chain travel.
  5. Adjust your swingarm tension bolts until you have exactly 25–30 mm of vertical chain slack at the midpoint of the swingarm. Tighten the main rear axle nut down.
4.3 — Lewis Brake Architecture
  1. Bolt the front brake rotor to the front wheel and the rear brake rotor to the rear hub using red Loctite on the small threads.
  2. Bolt the Lewis 6-Piston Caliper to the front fork adapter plate, and the Lewis 8-Piston Caliper to the rear swingarm brake bracket. Torque caliper brackets to 25–30 Nm.
  3. Route the brake lines up the forks and along the swingarm to the handlebars. Secure them with specialized line clips so they cannot touch the wheels or chain during full suspension compression.
  4. Fill the master cylinders with fresh DOT 4 or DOT 5.1 fluid. Attach a vacuum bleeder or use the traditional pump-and-hold method at the caliper bleed nipples until all air bubbles vanish and your brake levers feel rock-solid.

Stage 5 — Cockpit, Ergonomics & Bodywork Integration
5.1 — Handlebars & Display
  1. Secure the ROX 2" Pivot Risers into the KTM triple clamp bar mounts. Torque the bottom bolts to 20 Nm.
  2. Place the ProTaper EVO Handlebars into the risers. Rotate the bars to match your arm reach while sitting, then torque the upper riser clamps to 20 Nm in an X-pattern.
  3. Mount the 3.3 Display Screen directly to the center of the handlebars using its dedicated bracket. Connect the display communication data cable to the wire harness lead coming off the BAC8000.
  4. Slide on your throttle assembly, grips, switches, Warp9 Hand Guards and Under-Bar Mirrors.
5.2 — Seating & Plastics
  1. Mount the Warp9 Seat Riser firmly onto your modified Ultra Bee subframe assembly.
  2. Place the Guts Racing Husqvarna Seat (outfitted with the tall +30mm foam pad) onto the riser system, locking the forward tabs into place and bolting down the rear fastening points.
  3. Take your KTM 250 Gas Tank, remove any interior fuel petcocks or components, and hollow out the underside structural floor using a rotary tool or plastic saw until it drops cleanly over your top frame rail to act as a flip-up or removable battery cover lid.
  4. Align and bolt your Husqvarna Gold / KTM SX-F Plastics to the mounting bosses on the subframe and tank layout. Once happy with the overall visual alignment, snug down all the subframe bolts you left hand-tight in Step 1.2.
Stage 6 — High-Voltage Battery Deployment & Initial Startup

⚠️ HIGH VOLTAGE SAFETY: Put on insulated electrical gloves. Ensure the main circuit breaker on your battery pack is switched completely to OFF before handling.

  1. Lay down dense foam isolation pads along the inner walls and floor of the aluminum LBX battery tray. This keeps your custom 72V pack from wearing holes in itself against raw metal under rough trail conditions.
  2. Lower the 72V High-Output Battery Pack smoothly into the frame cavity. Ensure it sits entirely flat and no loose wires are trapped underneath it.
  3. Connect the heavy black negative (−) power lead from the BAC8000 to the negative terminal of the battery.
  4. Connect the heavy red positive (+) power lead to the positive battery terminal. Use insulated wrenches and torque the terminal nuts down tightly to prevent any electrical arcing.
  5. Secure your AirTag Security tracker out of sight by taping it inside a hollow structural cavity underneath the Guts seat foam or deep inside the wiring harness wrap.
  6. Install the Ultra Bee Headlight & Bezel to the front forks, connecting its input lead to your 12V DC-DC system regulator wire. Mount your Wireless Tail Lights & Signals to the rear fender extension.

Stage 7 — Pre-Flight Testing & Tuning Calibration

Before you put this machine on the ground, you must check its systems safely.

  1. Place the bike onto an off-road dirt bike stand so that both wheels are suspended completely off the ground.
  2. Connect your laptop or mobile tuning application to the BAC8000 Controller via your data link cable or Bluetooth adapter.
  3. Load your specific Sotion FW01 26–40kW motor profile map. Double-check that your phase current limits, voltage cutoffs, and pole-pair settings match the motor specs perfectly.
  4. Switch your main battery breaker to ON.
  5. Turn on the bike's ignition keyswitch. Ensure the 3.3 display boots up cleanly without throwing any error codes.
The Spin Test

Give the throttle a tiny, progressive nudge. Verify that:

  • The rear wheel rotates forward — if it rotates backward, toggle the "Reverse Motor Direction" setting in your BAC8000 software app.
  • The chain moves smoothly along the GritShift conversion kit without catching or binding.
  • There are no grinding noises coming from the Warp9 jackshaft or motor cradle.

Drop the bike off the stand, re-check your torque settings on the wheel axles and swingarm pivot, and perform a slow test ride to verify your alignment before opening up that massive 40kW power band.
